title: Dark Sector Flavor Symmetry: Gell-Mann–Okubo Mass Splittings for SU(3)dark Self-Interacting DM
content: Dark matter forms an octet under a hidden SU(3)dark flavor symmetry, and its mass spectrum obeys an extended Gell-Mann–Okubo formula with a negative hypercharge coefficient β = − 15 GeV the same sign that the strange quark imposes in QCD. The lightest neutral member χ0 sits at M(χ0) = 165.67 GeV ; every other state decays to it with Q ∈ [ 0.70,42.00 ] GeV, completing well before big bang nucleo-synthesis. A dark Higgs triplet ∆dark with ⟨∆dark⟩ = v∆ = 17 GeV breaks the χ+ – χ0 degeneracy that is unavoidable in the pure GMO spectrum, generating ∆M( χ+ – χ0) = yχv∆ = 1.70 GeV and opening χ+ → χ0 + ϕ+ with Q = 0.70 GeV . Eight coupled Boltzmann equations with Griest–Seckel co-annihilation ( geff ≈ 5.09) reproduce the measured relic density ΩDMh2 = 0.1200 ± 0.0012 at gdark = 0.64 ± 0.08, mZ′ = 17.5 ± 2.1 GeV . Elastic self-scattering via t-channel exchange of the broken-SU(3)dark vector Vµ (mV = 100 GeV ) yields σ/m ∝ v−2.1: 0.47 ± 0.09 cm2 g−1 at dwarf scales (resolving core-cusp and missing satellites) and 0.0044 ± 0.0009 cm2 g−1 at cluster scales (consistent with the Bullet Cluster). A partial Higgs–Stueckelberg mechanism absorbs seven of the eight would- be Goldstone bosons, giving ∆Neff ≈ 0.09; the surviving mode drives dark acoustic oscillations at rDAO = 2.3 ± 0.4 Mpc, within reach of SKA. The framework is falsifiable through twelve observables constrained by nine parameters. Two scale-independent mass ratios, r21 ≡ M(χ++) /M(χ0) = 1.089 ± 0.005 and \( r_{31} \equiv M(\Sigma^0_{\mathrm{dark}})/M(\chi^0) = 1.163\pm 0.006 \), are directly measurable at FCC-ee; their double ratio r21 /r 31 = 0.936 is independent of the overall mass scale. Either a detection or a null result at any of the twelve probes listed here constitutes a definitive test of dark-sector flavor symmetry.
